newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico markets down on Dow, not rebels - govt.
newsitem.headline: Mexico markets down on Dow, not rebels - govt.

text.p: The sharp sell-off on Mexico's markets on Thursday was due to profit-taking and weak U.S. markets more than the news of rebel attacks in southern Mexico, the Finance Ministry said in a statement.

"The negative session on the markets was due to several external factors, as well as profit-taking on the part of foreign investors in the United States ahead of Labor Day weekend," the ministry said in a statement.

Suprisingly strong U.S. Gross Domestic Product data sparked a sell-off on the Dow Jones and also pushed up long-term U.S. interest rates, drawing some money from emerging markets to higher returns in U.S. paper, the ministry said.
Mexican stocks fell 2.2 percent and the peso lost four centavos to 7.535/7.54 per dollar in 48-hour contracts.
But the Finance Ministry stressed that there was stability in the money market, where interest rates on same-day Cetes, or T-bills, closed down 150 basis points on Wednesday's close.

At the end of the statement, the Finance Ministry said the markets may also have been hit by other "political events" -- an indirect reference to news that leftist guerrillas killed at least 12 people in coordinated attacks in southern Mexico.

"In addition to the other factors mentioned, Mexican financial markets were affected by factors of a political nature, including news related to violent episodes that took place early today," it said.
